args.text: [lane-lynx] Three risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System) answers for too long: (1) Stale addresses: users are sent to a server that has moved or been retired, so pages fail or load the wrong service. (2) Slow recovery: when a site switches to a backup server during an outage, cached answers keep sending people to the broken one until the cache expires. (3) Prolonged poisoning: if a forged answer gets into the cache, it stays in place and misleads users for longer.

[lane-lynx] Idempotent (safe to repeat) retries matter because networks fail unpredictably, so a sender often cannot tell whether a request was received, and retrying is the only way to be sure it happens. If repeating the request has the same effect as sending it once, a retry cannot cause duplicate payments, orders or messages, so systems stay both reliable and correct.

[lane-lynx] Two trade-offs of UUIDv7 (Universally Unique Identifier, version 7) as a primary key: (1) It embeds a creation time, so anyone who sees an ID can tell roughly when the record was made, which may leak information. (2) It is 128 bits, larger than a typical 64-bit integer key, so indexes and related tables use more storage and memory, even though its time ordering keeps inserts far tidier than random UUIDs.
